sara-support: Hey — customer reports duplicate POSTs after SDK retry with undici + proxy. They see 2 requests with same idempotency key and billing double-charged. Happening intermittently, Node 18 on Heroku, undici@5.14.0, our ts-sdk 1.2.3.

alex: can you paste a minimal repro? also which proxy (http-proxy-agent?), any custom fetch override?

sara-support: repro below. note: we wrap request in AbortController with a timeout, then pass same controller into sdk.retries. sometimes abort triggers but a retry still sends another POST.

sara-support: ```ts
import fetch from 'undici'
const ac = new AbortController()
setTimeout(()=>ac.abort(), 250)
await sdk.request('/v1/generate',{method:'POST',body:payload,signal:ac.signal})
```

eng-qa: hmm — are you reusing the same AbortController across retry attempts? fetch will throw AbortError but SDK might start a fresh request with same signal if it's reused.

ryan: Node's fetch (undici) has weirdness where reusing signal across sequential requests can lead to immediate abort if previously aborted. Ensure you create a new signal per attempt or clone behavior. Also check keepAlive/proxy connection reuse: http-proxy-agent + undici sometimes doesn't close sockets predictably.

jordan: also check undici client version vs global fetch. If app bundles undici and Node runtime provides native fetch, you can end up with two implementations and mismatched AbortController classes. That causes signal instanceof checks to fail.

sara-support: oof, they are using globalThis.fetch = undici.fetch in app startup. Could that cause mismatch? stack trace shows "AbortError" from node:internal but SDK not recognizing.

alex: try this quick debug: 1) remove global override (use sdk's builtin fetch) 2) create fresh AbortController per attempt 3) disable SDK retries (set maxRetries:0) to confirm duplicate comes from retry logic

sara-support: tried disabling retries -> only one POST, but timed out and client returned error. With retries on, duplicate happens. So likely retry+signal reuse.

eng-qa: can you run with NODE_OPTIONS=--trace-warnings and dump undici version at runtime: ```js
console.log('undici', require('undici/package.json').version)
console.log('fetch', typeof globalThis.fetch)
```

sara-support: undici shows 5.14.0, global fetch = function. Node runtime is 18.17.1.

ryan: workaround: in SDK we should clone signals or create new AbortController per attempt. For now tell customer to avoid passing external signal to sdk.request; pass timeout via SDK's timeout option instead.

support-bot: Ticket #38421 created for billing duplicate-charge investigation. Assigned to eng-qa.

jordan: I'll open an internal issue: "ts-sdk: avoid reusing external AbortController across retries; normalize to SDK-owned timeout" and include repro. tagging infra to check proxy agent keep-alive.

sara-support: customer confirmed workaround (disable global fetch override + use SDK timeout) avoids duplicates. They want a patch in SDK so marking as high priority.

alex: thanks — please add short repro in the GH issue and paste logs (request ids, timestamps). I'll triage with eng-rt.

sara-support: done, uploaded reproducible test and logs to the ticket.

support-bot: Note: follow-up scheduled: eng-qa to validate fix on Node 18/20 and with http-proxy-agent.
